abstract: We share the commitment of Treves and colleagues1 to advancing human-wildlife coexistence and maintaining public trust in science and are grateful for the opportunity for further dialogue. We were asked to write a concise, introductory overview on human-wildlife conflict that was general enough to not require citations, orienting non-specialists to key concepts. The Current Biology primer format limits the nuance that experts in the field might desire. We agree that science benefits from the exploration of alternative hypotheses and agree that in-line citations would have allowed us to make more specific, evidence-based claims.
